claims.text: The initial NbZrTiHfMo alloy is equiatomic.
The as-cast NbZrTiHfMo alloy is a disordered, single-phase BCC refractory high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast alloy has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of approximately 1719 MPa.
The as-cast alloy has limited ductility.
Cold rolling to approximately 80% thickness reduction followed by annealing at about 700 °C for 20 minutes can restore ductility without a major loss of compressive strength.
Heavy cold rolling induces work hardening through increased dislocation density and grain refinement.
Cold-rolling-induced work hardening increases strength but reduces ductility.
Annealing the heavily rolled alloy at approximately 700 °C for 20 minutes will produce partial recovery.
The proposed annealing treatment will produce limited, necklace-type recrystallization.
Partial recovery and limited recrystallization will reduce dislocation tangles and low- or medium-angle grain boundaries.
The moderate anneal will preserve a substantial portion of the cold-work-induced dislocation density.
Intrinsic lattice distortion and retained dislocation structures contribute to the alloy's high strength.
Partial recrystallization and dislocation rearrangement will relieve localized stresses and improve plastic deformation.
Solid-solution strengthening and residual dislocation structures will preserve high yield strength after annealing.
The rolled-and-annealed alloy will sustain greater compressive plastic strain before failure than the rolled, unannealed alloy.
The rolled-and-annealed alloy will retain a compressive yield strength close to the as-cast value of 1719 MPa.
Annealing at substantially lower temperatures may provide insufficient recovery.
Annealing at substantially higher temperatures may cause full recrystallization and sacrifice strengthening dislocation structures.
